title: Twists are well-defined on the common-finite-stage coefficient category
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $S$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], fix $m\in\mathbf Z$, and let $\mathcal C_S=D^b_c(S,\Qlb)$ be the common-stage category of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. For each finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ contained in $\Qlb$, let $T_{E,m}$ be the rational twist functor induced on integral representatives by tensoring with $\mathcal O_E(m)$ [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Assume the finite-stage inverse identities $T_{E,-m}T_{E,m}\cong\mathrm{id}$ and $T_{E,m}T_{E,-m}\cong\mathrm{id}$ given by line evaluation. Write $B_{F/E}$ for scalar extension from $E$ to $F$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and use the natural comparisons $\beta_{F/E,C}:B_{F/E}(T_{E,m}C)\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{F,m}(B_{F/E}C)$ of [lem-weil-integral-twist-derived-scalar] after rationalization. Assume their identity and tower compatibility of [lem-weil-integral-twist-scalar-coherence] and their compatibility with line evaluation of [lem-weil-integral-twist-base-change], for $m$ and $-m$. Then the assignment $(E,C)\mapsto(E,T_{E,m}C)$ defines a functor on $\mathcal C_S$: for a representative $[F,f]:(E,C)\to(E',C')$, where $f:B_{F/E}C\to B_{F/E'}C'$, its image is represented by
$$
 [F,\,\beta_{F/E',C'}^{-1}\circ T_{F,m}(f)\circ\beta_{F/E,C}].
$$
Equivalently it is $[F,T_{F,m}(f)]$ after identifying the endpoints by $\beta$. This class is independent of enlarging $F$, and composition is preserved. The line-evaluation inverse identities descend through these same comparisons. The resulting functor $T_m:\mathcal C_S\to\mathcal C_S$ has inverse $T_{-m}$, so $\Qlb(m)$ is invertible in the common-stage category.

proof.text: Bundle T_s and b_s as a StageSystem.Morphism F_s on the stage system of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]; its coh field is exactly the supplied tower hypothesis. Use the already proved upstream StageSystem.Morphism.functor, whose mapAt formula is b_source.hom followed by T_s(f) followed by b_target.inv. Its quotient construction and tr_mapAt lemma establish independence under enlargement and both functor laws. The requested object equality and representative HEq are definitional equalities.

For each sign form the morphism of stage systems F_s.comp F_not_s. Its comparison is b_not_s at T_s(C), followed by T_not_s(b_s at C). The finite evaluation homomorphisms e_s,E.hom give a StageSystem.Morphism.Hom from this composite to the identity morphism: unfolding comp and id reduces its comm square to the symmetric supplied evaluation-compatibility equation. Thus StageSystem.Morphism.descNatTrans gives the evaluation on the pair category. Its components are the stage-inclusion images of the finite evaluation components.

Each e_s,E is a natural isomorphism, so the proved StageSystem.Morphism.isIso_descNatTrans makes the descended evaluation invertible. Compose the inverse of functorCompIso, asIso of the descended evaluation, and functorIdIso to obtain U_s followed by U_not_s isomorphic to the identity. The composition and identity comparison components are identities, so simplification leaves precisely the stated stage-inclusion image of e_s,E at each pair. This works for both signs at once, including repeated stages and m=0; all tensor normalization assumptions are preserved in the unchanged statement.

Shape: one commit; proof_deps equals the union of the step uses; no cycle (the parent cites the item, the item does not cite the parent); no SGA source. Coefficient category: the raw common-stage Hom colimit of def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients and the raw rationalization, with no Karoubi completion. The coherence lemma says its a_C rationalizes to the lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition associator, so Step 2's a is the Hom-system transition. I checked every step by explicit composition. Step 2: both rearrangements of the tower equation are correct, sources and targets included. Step 3: with β_{G/F} naturality the enlargement of t_F(f) equals t_G(f^G), which gives representative independence. Step 4: identity and composition hold. Step 5: γ is well typed, and e_F∘γ = B(e_E) is the assumed evaluation-compatibility hypothesis written out termwise. Step 6: expanding twice gives γ'^{-1}T_{-m}T_m(f)γ, and the naturality square and inverse components follow. Step 7: E(m)=T_{E,m}(E_S), and invertibility at Q̄ is read as in the parent's statement. Edge cases m=0, m<0, E=E', F=E and unrelated E, E' all go through. No duplicate found (lem-weil-twist-rationalization covers only the rational stage; det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-twists and lem-sf-twist-interchange are about other things).
